anne-ml: Quick heads-up: after enabling FP8 KV in nightly builds, I'm seeing a p99 latency spike on long-context chat workloads (~12k tokens). Memory churn goes up too. Anyone else seeing this?

raj-runtime: Yep, reproduced locally on rtx-a100-sim. p99 up ~12-18% depending on batch. Attached short profiler snippet.

maria-sre: I noticed host CPU activity spiking during decode. Looks like a lot of memcpy/page-fault churn around the gather path. Could be alignment or an extra copy.

kevin-ops: nvprof excerpt I grabbed (trimmed):
```
GPU activities:
  kv_gather_fp8_kernel    12.3ms
  kv_gather_int8_kernel    5.1ms
  decode_step_fp32_kernel  7.8ms  <-- fallback observed when batch>8
CPU memcpy (host):        18ms (per batch, spikes)
```
Seems kernel selection is choosing a higher-latency path in some batched cases.

jin-rl: Quality reg: small decoding drifts in a couple of convo prompts — tokens diverge after ~40 tokens (repeats/odd phrasing). Example diff: expected: "I'll schedule the meeting for 3pm." got: "I'll schedule the meeting on 3pm, ok?" Not huge but consistent for some intents.

anne-ml: Hypothesis: FP8 KV uses a tighter packed layout that breaks our 128B alignment assumption. Batching heuristics + kernel-selection heuristic then trigger an extra host-side rewrite to align pages, which costs CPU and increases latency. Also calibration mismatch could nudge layernorm/scaling leading to small quality drift.

raj-runtime: Ran microbench (isolated kv_gather):
```
# bench script
for b in 1 4 8 16; do run_kv_bench --layout fp8 --batch $b; done
# results (median)
batch=1: 1.8ms
batch=4: 3.6ms
batch=8: 6.8ms
batch=16: 14.2ms  <-- big jump, host memcpy + kernel fallback
```
memcpy throughput drops ~30% with batch=16+ when FP8 layout enabled.

kevin-ops: Quick mitigation: force int8 gather for batches >= 8 or update scheduler to prefer kernels that avoid host-copy. I'll prototype a small scheduler patch. :+1:

maria-sre: For safety, rolling FP8 KV out of nightly until patch lands. ci-bot: please block FP8-KV flag on canary.

ci-bot: Build pipelines updated: flag fp8_kv = OFF for nightly and canary channels.

deploy-bot: Rollback performed to commit 45f3a2d on /runtime/nightly at 2026-03-18T15:12Z. Monitoring.

anne-ml: Action items: raj-runtime - add KV microbench into perf suite and add a kernel-selection unit test. kevin-ops - PR to prefer int8 for small-batch or fix alignment and memcpy elimination. jin-rl - run quality evals on 50 prompt set to quantify drift. I'll schedule the re-enable window Friday noon.

jin-rl: Quick eval numbers (conversation subset of 50 prompts):
- baseline (int8 KV): ppl 12.4, 3 regressions with minor token phrasing
- fp8 KV (pre-rollback): ppl 13.0, 8 regressions including 2 intent-breaking cases
Not catastrophic but correlated with the large-batch mem path.

raj-runtime: Repro script gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/kv-fuzz-2061234567 (includes seed, batch patterns, and perf counters).

kevin-ops: Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1234 — scheduler: prefer int8-gather for batch sizes that trigger host-copy; also attempt 128B align pad for FP8 layout to avoid memcpy. Will request review.

anne-ml: Nice. Please also emit tracing event when we choose a kernel that requires host-copy so we can correlate in prod dashboards. Ping me when PR is ready for review. Thanks everyone.
